integrity.chow_divisor_basis: The inspected archival note defines the Chow hypersurface as the Grassmannian locus of linear spaces intersecting the projective cycle.
integrity.first_public_date_basis: The foundational Duke Mathematical Journal article has verified publication date 1992-07-01. A 1991 proceedings note cites an earlier January 1991 technical report without a day; no day was invented for that earlier source.
integrity.fixed_point_basis: A generic intrinsic cocharacter separates the monomial weights, so Grassmannian fixed points are coordinate subspaces and toric fixed points are coordinate vertices of the weight polytope.
integrity.localization_basis: Topological Euler characteristic of a projective complex variety with an algebraic C* action equals that of its fixed locus.
integrity.primary_slot_basis: The bibliographic classification for Chow polytopes and general resultants lists 14M25 first, followed by 14C05 and 52B20.
integrity.toric_basis: The same source treats projective toric varieties as closures of monomial torus orbits determined by a lattice-point configuration.

scientific_limitations: Only ordinary Euler characteristic of the projective Chow divisor and compactly supported Euler characteristic of its complement are computed.
The theorem does not determine Betti or Hodge numbers, singularities, the Chow-form degree, or the Chow polytope.
The short fixed-point proof leaves a residual risk of an unindexed or folklore equivalent.
title: Euler characteristic of toric Chow divisors depends only on ambient size and polytope vertices
